visual.general_description: Axial lung-window chest CT slice with multiple soft-tissue nodules in both lungs and one white arrow near the hilum.
visual.detailed_description: Single unlettered grayscale axial chest CT image in lung window, with no orientation letters, scale bar, patient text or measurements. Both aerated lungs are dark with vessels and bronchi; the spine is at the bottom and the anterior chest wall at the top. In the image-left lung there is a perihilar soft-tissue opacity with branching airways, a rounded well-defined opacity at the lateral mid-lung and smaller round nodules at the lower lateral lung, plus several thin-walled air-filled cystic lucencies in the upper lung. In the image-right lung a large lobulated soft-tissue opacity lies in the posterior lung near the hilum with internal linear lucent (airway or vessel) structures, and other smaller opacities are present. One white arrow in the image-left perihilar opacity points to a tiny punctate bright focus. No other arrows or annotations; no pleural effusion or pneumothorax is distinguishable in this slice.

visual.general_description: Frontal chest radiograph with a large speckled mass-like opacity at the right lung base, three smaller arrowed opacities on the image-right side, and an implanted device on the image-right chest wall.
visual.detailed_description: Single unlettered grayscale frontal chest radiograph with no orientation letters, scale or printed measurements. A large oval opacity with coarse mottled/speckled high-density (calcific-appearing) texture occupies the image-left lower lung zone; a white arrow marks its upper margin. On the image-right side there are three more white arrows: one at a small faint round opacity in the upper-mid lung just below an implanted pulse-generator-like device, one at the cardiac border region, and one near the lower lung/diaphragm. A battery/electronics device lies over the image-right upper chest wall with two leads running medially and downward toward the heart, and midline sternal wire loops are visible. Calcification of the three smaller arrowed opacities cannot be judged at this resolution.

visual.general_description: Axial soft-tissue-window chest CT with a large densely calcified mass at the anterior chest wall on the image-left and a small dense nodule posteriorly on the image-right, each marked by an arrow.
visual.detailed_description: Single unlettered grayscale axial chest CT in soft-tissue window with no orientation letters, scale or printed measurements; the lungs appear uniformly black without parenchymal detail. A large lobulated mass abutting the anterior-lateral chest wall and the cardiac border on the image-left contains dense coarse/speckled bone-density calcifications; a white arrow marks its anteromedial margin. On the image-right posterior, adjacent to the descending aorta and spine, a small elongated dense calcified nodule is marked by a second white arrow. Several very bright metallic-density foci with radiating streak artifacts lie in the anterior mediastinum/cardiac region, and metallic densities are visible at the sternum. The heart, vertebral body, ribs and both arms are visible.

The ascending aorta, pulmonary trunk and descending aorta are bright. A single dense, well-circumscribed, lobulated round nodule lies in the posterior image-right lung abutting the posterior pleural surface; it is saturated white, markedly brighter than the adjacent vessels and soft tissue, and a white arrow points to it. Tiny bright dots near it and elsewhere are vessels or small foci. The remaining lung parenchyma in this slice looks clear; no pneumothorax, chest tube, surgical staple line or pleural effusion is visible, and no other large nodules are seen.
